beginner.headline: Canoes is small, but a peaking 16-second SSW swell can push sets and current through the inside. Watch full set cycles before you start.
beginner.recommendation: Inspect Canoes about 8:30–9:00 AM. Run a normal first-time adult lesson if Inside Canoes stays about 1–2 ft and post-set current stays manageable.
reasons: Broader South Shore energy is well up
Inside set penetration and current decide the final call
precheck: Check how far a real set moves you, and the post-set current
decisive: Student profile and number of students
no_go: Repeated larger sets washing through the inside
Brown, gray, cloudy or turbid water

general.headline: Peaking south swell. Exposed Town breaks are the call for competent intermediate to advanced surfers.
general.size_note: Regional South Shore forecast: 5–7 ft morning, 6–8 ft afternoon. Not Canoes.
general.waikiki_note: Protected Waikīkī stays small. Longboards and high-volume boards.

canoes.note: Break-specific estimate. Surf quality and lesson suitability are rated separately: small, protected Canoes can still be good for teaching.

regional.scope: Oʻahu south-facing shores. Does not apply directly to Canoes.

effects: Bigger gap between sets and average waves
swell.warning: Long-period sets can push much harder than the 1–2 ft average suggests.

wind.note: Wind is a secondary limit today.

positives: More room in the teaching zone
tide.conflict: The tide improves while the long-period swell stays near peak.
tide.rule: High tide is not automatically the best lesson time. Combine tide with swell, current, wind and the student.

current.field_test: Watch how far you and the student are moved by one complete real set, and how much work it takes to get back in position.
current.one_student: Higher tolerance. You can shadow and manage drift.
current.multi_student: Lower tolerance: separation, more retrieval, less control. If current is strong, split the group, take one at a time, or reschedule.

windows.label: Best available
reasons: Ahead of the afternoon regional peak
notes: Wave impact low, occasional moderate sets

windows.label: Conditional to avoid
reasons: More current and sets reaching the inside
avoid_for: Several students if current is significant

avoid_triggers: Repeated powerful sets reaching Inside Canoes
effort_rule: Your workload can't be read from wave height alone. Goal: more surfing, less paddling.

boards.town: Competent intermediate to advanced. 3–4+ ft at the breaks, 5–8 ft regional exposed-shore forecast.

upcoming.note: No flood watch yet. Forecast confidence isn't high enough for one.

watch.head: South Shore surf near advisory level
watch.body: Surf is expected to approach High Surf Advisory criteria. No advisory is active.

watch.head: Wet stretch Wednesday night to Friday
watch.body: Tropical moisture, locally heavy rain and isolated thunderstorms possible. Runoff can follow heavy rain.

hazards.name: High surf advisory, South Shore
hazards.note: Near advisory level is not an active advisory.

tropical.note: No active Central Pacific cyclones. Nolo has left the Central Pacific. Today's south swell is Southern Hemisphere groundswell, not Nolo.

water.headline: No Waikīkī advisory verified
water.statement: No Waikīkī or Canoes-specific water-quality advisory was verified during this refresh.
water.why: The live DOH Clean Water Branch advisory list couldn't be read this run, so statewide and Oʻahu notices are unknown.
water.runoff: Brown, gray, cloudy or turbid water, or visible runoff: don't go in, advisory or not.

gaps: Live DOH advisory list couldn't be read
